authoredPrompt: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for time t: the learner drags a marker along the logistic curve, the population value, tangent slope, and distance below y = c update together, making clear that growth is fastest at c/2 and slows as carrying capacity is approached.
- Slider for growth rate b: the learner increases or decreases b, the S-curve becomes steeper or flatter and the labeled maximum-growth point shifts horizontally, showing how b controls the timing and intensity of the transition toward saturation.
authoredContext:
The graph in the figure shows how the growth rate changes over time. The graph increases from left to right, but the growth rate only increases until it reaches its point of maximum growth rate, at which point the rate of increase decreases.

Graph of f(t)=c/(1+ae^(-tx)). The carrying capacity is the asymptote at y=c. The initial value of population is (0, c/(1+a)). The point of maximum growth is (ln(a)/b, c/2).

evaluation.notes: The main logistic-growth structure, dashed carrying-capacity line, axes, points, and annotations are mostly faithful, but the huge curve arrowheads and cramped initial-value annotation noticeably reduce visual fidelity.

Render the logistic formula as a clearer fraction-style label, or at least increase spacing and legibility so it more closely matches the source.
